newsitem.title: GERMANY: German who killed policeman was far right extremist.
newsitem.headline: German who killed policeman was far right extremist.

text.p: German prosecutors said on Monday a 24-year-old Berlin man who shot and killed a police officer during a routine traffic inspection was a right-wing extremist and "armed for war".

A 34-year-old police officer was killed and a second officer seriously wounded on Sunday when the heavily armed 24-year-old opened fire on the two after they had approached his car at a motorway rest stop east of Hamburg.
The suspect, later captured after a chase and shootout with police, was driving a car filled with munitions.
"He was armed for war," said Gunter Moeller, state prosecutor in Luebeck. "It is possible that the suspect saw in the police and the state his mortal enemy."

Justice authorities in Berlin were investigating whether the suspect might also have been responsible for the shooting of a book dealer in Berlin last week. The dealer, whose business is in a building also used by the communist Party of Democratic Socialism (PDS), was seriously injured.
Ruediger Reiff, justice ministry spokesman in Berlin, said the suspect's residence was close to the scene of the crime. He said a similar weapon was used for both shootings.
